summary: Frontend-only test iter 12. Verified 7 requested flows against deployed preview. PASS: (a) login as testwriter@example.com/testpass123, (b) sidebar Projects tab → Scenes pencil rename → Enter saves + persists across full reload, (c) sidebar Projects tab → double-click scene row opens same inline input, Escape reverts, (d) history session double-click rename (Sessions tab → history-item-<id> dblclick → history-rename-input-<id> → Enter) updates row label, (e) delete-user-0 edge case: clicking mode-turn-user-0-delete on a passage bubble clears mode-passage-view (toast 'Passage cleared') and the assistant reply remains rendered (re-indexed to mode-turn-assistant-0). FAIL: (1) A-/A+ font-size persistence — in-memory works (initial=18, dec→15, inc→20, min-bound=13, max-bound=26, disabled states correct), but PUT /api/settings returns 422 ('Field required: user_id') because backend Pydantic Settings model requires user_id while the frontend never sends it. Result: font_size does NOT survive page reload — reload restores server-stored value (18), regressing user-selected size. (2) Per-bubble delete on Jupiter assistant bubble — mode-turn-assistant-1-delete fires the confirm dialog and toasts 'Turn deleted', but the bubble is NOT fully removed. Pre-delete assistant text = 768 chars; after one accepted delete, mode-turn-assistant-1 still exists with 607 chars starting mid-word ('t closer to honest…'). Cause is in parseTranscript/serializeTurns roundtrip in ModeWorkspace.jsx: the LLM's initial reply contains the sentinel marker '──── jupiter ────' (or an em-dash sequence that matches the split regex), so a single actual assistant reply is parsed into multiple assistant turns; deleting turnIndex 1 removes only one slice and re-indexes the next slice into position 1 again. Repeated clicks progressively chop the reply.

critical.issue: Returns 422 'Field required: user_id' for every settings save because backend Pydantic Settings model requires user_id but the frontend PUT body never includes it. Blocks ALL settings persistence including the new font_size A-/A+ control. Fix: make user_id optional on the request model (server-injects from auth cookie) OR have frontend inject user_id from /auth/me.

ui_bugs.issue: Deleting mode-turn-assistant-1 does not fully remove the assistant bubble — bubble persists with a truncated, mid-word fragment. Root cause: parseTranscript splits on '──── jupiter ────' / '──── you ────' sentinel markers; when the assistant reply itself contains one of those substrings (Jupiter frequently emits similar dashed section headers), a single reply is parsed as multiple assistant turns, so filtering one turn leaves the others rendering at the same testid index.
Font-size selection does not persist across reload because the underlying PUT /api/settings returns 422 (see backend). In-memory bounds & disabled states are correct.

integration_issues.issue: Every debounced settings PUT returns 422; console shows repeated 'Failed to load resource: 422' errors. No user-visible error surfaces because the .catch(() => {}) in settings.jsx swallows the failure.

action_items: Backend: Make Settings.user_id server-side only (either not required on request body, or use a separate SettingsUpdate model without user_id) so PUT /api/settings succeeds. This will unblock font_size persistence.

Frontend ModeWorkspace: Fix parseTranscript/serializeTurns so an assistant reply that legitimately contains dashed section headers is not mis-split. Options: (a) use a more unique sentinel like '\u0000JUPITER-TURN-BOUNDARY\u0000' that the LLM cannot emit, (b) store turns as a structured array in state instead of a single serialized string, (c) escape the sentinel when appending assistant text.
Frontend settings.jsx: Surface the 422 to the user (toast) instead of swallowing — silent failures made this bug invisible for iterations.
Optional: bubble delete button uses opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 — fine for desktop but unreachable on touch devices; consider adding focus-within or a tap-to-reveal alternative.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py Settings model requires user_id on the request payload — this is a classic Pydantic footgun. Split into SettingsIn (no user_id) and SettingsOut (with user_id) so the request model matches what the client sends.
frontend/src/lib/settings.jsx swallows all PUT failures with .catch(() => {}) — this masked a persistent 422 for at least this iteration. Add toast.error or at minimum console.error.

frontend/src/components/ModeWorkspace.jsx parseTranscript relies on a plaintext sentinel that the LLM's own output can accidentally reproduce; storing the conversation as a serialized string with human-readable delimiters is fragile. Migrate to a structured turns[] state (persist as JSON) and serialize only when writing to /api/ai/history.
frontend/src/components/ChatBubble.jsx onDelete button is opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 — invisible/unreachable on touch. Consider always visible on mobile viewport.

Sidebar rename testids follow inconsistent naming — pencil is data-testid='rename-page-<id>' but the input is 'page-rename-input-<id>' and the row is 'page-item-<id>'. The review request called the pencil 'page-rename-btn-<id>' — either normalise to page-rename-btn-<id> for consistency with history-rename-btn-<id>, or update docs. Not a bug, but a maintainability concern.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The two failing flows are independent: (1) Settings 422 is a backend-model bug — fix Settings model to not require user_id on PUT body (server injects from get_current_user_id dependency). (2) Assistant delete is a parseTranscript bug — reproduce by running Collaborate with any non-trivial passage (LLM often emits '──── jupiter ────'-like dashed section headers); check if mode-turn-assistant-1 still exists after clicking mode-turn-assistant-1-delete and dialog.accept(). Preferred fix is structured turns[] state instead of stringly-typed serialization. Selectors verified working: mode-passage-view (not mode-passage-input as the review request said), rename-page-<id> (pencil, not page-rename-btn-<id>), page-rename-input-<id>, page-item-<id>, history-item-<id>, history-rename-input-<id>, font-size-{control,decrease-btn,increase-btn,value}, mode-turn-{user,assistant}-<n>[-delete]. Confirm dialogs: use page.on('dialog', async d: d.accept()) — verified working (dialog message 'Remove this turn?' captured).
rca of the issue: Bug 1 (settings 422): backend/server.py:163 defines Settings(BaseModel) with user_id: str (no default) and the PUT endpoint declares body: Settings. Frontend never sends user_id (settings.jsx line 46: api.put('/settings', settings) where settings state omits user_id). FastAPI validation rejects with 422 before the endpoint runs. Fix: create SettingsIn(BaseModel) without user_id or with user_id: Optional[str] = None; use it as the request body; keep Settings for storage. Bug 2 (assistant delete leaves fragment): ModeWorkspace.jsx stores conversations as a single serialized string with sentinel markers '──── you ────' and '──── jupiter ────'. LLM output frequently contains em-dash sequences that trigger the split regex, causing a single logical reply to be parsed as multiple assistant turns at the same visible index. Deleting turn N filters one but the next survivor promotes to index N and remains data-testid='mode-turn-assistant-1'. Fix: replace the string-based store with a turns[] array state and serialize only for /api/ai/history persistence, OR use a control-character sentinel that cannot appear in LLM output.
